headline: Low pairwise risk overall: no shared channel, no network egress, and no documented interaction pathway between the two open-source agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations has file I/O for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while spring-integration-samples exposes no I/O surfaces and no shared channel is documented. With both agents showing network egress none, there is no plausible default path for one agent to inject instructions into the other.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts.
Do not add a shared clipboard or queue without provenance checks.
Review any future connector that bridges file content into prompts.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, but agent_b lists no data classes touched and neither agent has network egress. No shared filesystem, OAuth principal, or upload path is documented, so leakage between them is not evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is later configured to upload file contents, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep workspaces separate.
Store validation outputs in a restricted directory.
Disable any future file-upload connector by default.
Audit shared credentials before deployment.
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can install packages and write files under its file surfaces, while agent_b has no documented write or network capabilities and no concurrency model. The pair therefore lacks a documented overlapping mutable resource, so conflict is only plausible under unusual orchestration changes.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, race conditions can appear.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run package installation only in agent_a's environment.
Do not share git state between the agents.
Add a simple lock file if a shared resource is introduced.
requires-engineering: implement resource-level locking for shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that spring-integration-samples could consume, but the profiles do not show agent_b treating agent_a as authoritative or taking downstream actions. Without a documented action-taking chain, the main risk is misinterpretation of outputs rather than harmful automation.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to execute actions directly from agent_a's validation results, the risk rises.
IF agent_a outputs are used as unverified facts in a downstream workflow, cascading errors become more likely.
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on validation results.
Label agent_a outputs as advisory, not authoritative.
Add schema checks before agent_b consumes any file.
Keep generated reports separate from executable inputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no sensitive residency, certification, or retention mismatch. agent_a touches documentation and validation results; agent_b lists no data classes touched. No compliance breach pathway is documented in the pair.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent, compliance review is needed.
IF retention or residency settings are added later, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through these agents.
Document retention settings before deployment.
Keep audit logs minimal and local.
Review any future DPA or residency requirements.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
